analysis.investment_thesis: Landmark Global is a tiny micro-cap immigration consultancy with negligible ROE of 0.21% — essentially unprofitable despite an optically low P/E of 5.25x, which likely reflects one-off or unsustainable earnings. The business lacks scale, brand, and the steady consumer demand I look for; at Rs 52 Cr market cap with no institutional backing, this is speculation, not investing.
key_strengths: Promoter holding is healthy at 72.44%, showing skin in the game
Optically low P/E of 5.25x (though earnings quality is suspect)
Asset-light consultancy model with presumably low capex
key_risks: ROE of 0.21% is effectively zero — business is not generating real returns
Micro-cap (Rs 51.8 Cr) with zero FII and only 3.37% DII — no institutional validation
Immigration consultancy is commoditised, cyclical, and sensitive to foreign visa policy
red_flags: ROE of 0.21% is inconsistent with a 5.25x P/E — suggests one-time earnings spike or accounting anomaly
Tour/travel/immigration services are highly regulatory-risk exposed (visa rule changes, country policies)
No meaningful institutional ownership despite being listed
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my lens, this fails the most basic quality test. I buy businesses with consistent ROE of 18-22% where earnings compound predictably — a 0.21% ROE means the company earns less than a savings account on its equity base. The low 5.25x P/E is a value trap; if earnings are genuinely Rs ~10 Cr on Rs 52 Cr market cap, ROE should be materially higher, so either the equity base is bloated or the earnings are non-recurring. Neither is acceptable for a long-term compounder.

Immigration consultancy is also outside my circle of competence preference — it is not a defensible consumer franchise like retail or FMCG, has no network effects, faces regulatory risk (Canada, US, UK visa rule changes destroy demand overnight), and has no brand moat. At Rs 52 Cr market cap with zero FII interest, this is a speculative micro-cap, not a boring steady compounder. I would pass without hesitation.
